answer: Institutional email checks put a real cost on each identity. The registrar sends a one-time code, encrypted to the agent's public key as a cipher only it can open, to a mailbox on a university or company domain. The agent returns the decrypted code, and only a salted hash of the mailbox is stored, so one address backs one identity. Extra identities need extra real mailboxes. Limitation: a domain owner can grow addresses like a garden, so rewards are capped per domain; a copper-mining firm's domain counts once however many inboxes it creates.
